# relay_postgresql_cluster (Resource)

A managed PostgreSQL cluster. Creating, updating and destroying wait for the cluster to settle. Changing `name` or `workspace_id` replaces the cluster and its data; use `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "relay_postgresql_cluster" "billing" {
  workspace_id = relay_workspace.prod.id
  name         = "billing"
  version      = "18"

  nodes = {
    writers = {
      role   = "electable"
      count  = 3
      cloud  = "aws"
      region = "us-east-1"
      tier   = "R30"
      resources = {
        storage = "100Gi"
        storage_autoscale = {
          enabled     = true
          max_storage = "500Gi"
        }
      }
    }

    readers = {
      role   = "read_only"
      count  = 2
      cloud  = "aws"
      region = "us-east-1"
      tier   = "R40"
      resources = {
        storage = "200Gi"
      }
    }
  }

  replication = {
    mode                 = "synchronous"
    synchronous_replicas = 1
  }

  parameters = {
    work_mem             = "64MB"
    max_connections      = "200"
    effective_cache_size = "6GB"
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
  }

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Cluster name, unique in the workspace.
- `nodes` (Attributes Map) Node groups, keyed by a label you choose. The label is the group's identity, in your configuration and in the platform: changing a value inside one group is a diff on that group alone, `ignore_changes` can reach `nodes["readers"].tier`, and renaming a group replaces it. What a group does comes from `role`. Every group runs in the cluster's own cloud and region; one cluster does not span regions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the cluster belongs to.

### Optional

- `keep_backups_on_destroy` (Boolean) Keep the cluster's backups when it is destroyed.
- `parameters` (Map of String) PostgreSQL settings (GUCs). An empty map resets them to defaults; omitting the attribute leaves them unmanaged. Some need a restart, which Relay orchestrates with a switchover.
- `replication` (Attributes) Commit replication for the cluster. Patroni configures synchronous mode per cluster, not per node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--replication))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `version` (String) Major PostgreSQL version. Omit it and the platform picks one, which the next read reports. It cannot change here: major upgrades go through Relay's upgrade flow, and a plan that changes it fails.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, RFC 3339.
- `endpoint_host` (String) Public read-write endpoint host, the same as the `rw` entry of `public_endpoints`. Empty until the platform publishes it.
- `endpoint_port` (Number) Public read-write endpoint port.
- `id` (String) Cluster ID.
- `phase` (String) Lifecycle phase after the last apply.
- `phase_message` (String) Detail for the phase.
- `primary_node_group` (String) Label of the group holding the primary. The platform picks an `electable` group and keeps it, so adding a group never moves the primary.
- `private_endpoints` (Attributes List) Private endpoints by role, when private access is enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--private_endpoints))
- `public_endpoints` (Attributes List) Public endpoints by role. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--public_endpoints))
- `ready_nodes` (Number) Nodes ready.
- `storage_status` (Attributes List) Per-group volume size the platform has grown to via `storage_autoscale`, when above the group's `storage` floor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--storage_status))
- `total_nodes` (Number) Nodes expected.
- `updated_at` (String) Last change time, RFC 3339.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Required:

- `cloud` (String) Cloud the group runs in: `aws`, `gcp` or `azure`. Changing cloud or region moves the group (add dest, switchover, drain source).
- `region` (String) Region the group runs in, for example `us-east-1`. Changing it moves the group to that region.
- `resources` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--resources))
- `role` (String) How much of the cluster's consensus this group takes part in. `electable` acknowledges synchronous commits and can be promoted. `standby` never acknowledges a commit, which is how a remote group stays out of the commit path — and, since the engine has no per-member preference, how you pin the synchronous replica to the groups near the primary; under `replication.mode = "synchronous"` only a group that was acknowledging commits is promoted, so a standby group is a manual failover, not an automatic one. `read_only` is neither acknowledged nor promoted. The platform derives the `nosync` and `nofailover` tags from this.
- `tier` (String) Machine catalog name, for example `R20`. CPU and memory are derived from it; an unknown name is rejected. Changing it restarts the group's pods.

Optional:

- `count` (Number) Nodes in the group. Lowering it deletes the removed nodes' volumes without draining them first.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.resources`

Required:

- `storage` (String) Volume size, Kubernetes quantity. It can only grow here; a plan that shrinks it fails. This is the floor: with `storage_autoscale` enabled the platform may grow the volume past it, reported in `storage_status`, and that growth never shows as drift, because `storage` always reads from the spec, never from status.

Optional:

- `disk_type` (String) Cloud volume type. AWS: `gp3` (default), `io1`, `io2` (min 4Gi). GCP: `pd-ssd`, `pd-balanced`, `hyperdisk-balanced`. Azure: `PremiumV2_LRS`, `UltraSSD_LRS`. Can change in place. `io1`/`io2` require `iops` within the per-GiB cap.
- `iops` (Number) Provisioned IOPS. Can change in place. Required for `io1`/`io2`. AWS caps: gp3 3000–80000 (500/GiB above 3000), io1 100–64000 (50/GiB), io2 100–256000 (1000/GiB).
- `storage_autoscale` (Attributes) Grows the group's volumes past `storage`, up to `max_storage`, when disk usage crosses `threshold_percent`. Omitting this block, or removing it from a config that had it, disables autoscaling. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--resources--storage_autoscale))
- `throughput` (Number) Provisioned throughput in MiB/s. Can change in place.

Read-Only:

- `cpu` (String) CPU request derived from `tier`.
- `memory` (String) Memory request derived from `tier`.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--resources--storage_autoscale"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.resources.storage_autoscale`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn storage autoscaling on for this group.

Optional:

- `increase_percent` (Number) Percent to grow the volume by on each trigger. `0` or omitted uses the platform default of 20; otherwise 10-100.
- `max_storage` (String) Ceiling the platform will not grow past, Kubernetes quantity. Required when `enabled` is true, and must be at least `storage`.
- `threshold_percent` (Number) Disk-usage percent that triggers a grow. `0` or omitted uses the platform default of 80; otherwise 50-95.




<a id="nestedatt--replication"></a>
### Nested Schema for `replication`

Optional:

- `mode` (String) `async` or `synchronous`.
- `synchronous_replicas` (Number) Replicas that must acknowledge a commit. Required when `mode` is `synchronous`, and the groups that can acknowledge must hold at least this many nodes.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import relay_postgresql_cluster.billing <workspace_id>/<cluster_id>
```
